BLOCKER: Migration grandfathering predicate is still non-deterministic: "items created before cutoff" does not pin the source of item creation time (backlog file first git commit? ctime? id-block?). This reintroduces the same void-the-invariant loophole CL flagged; without a single authoritative field, any legacy MATERIAL_CHANGE approval can be claimed as grandfathered, defeating AC-2 ordering.

content_policy is a denylist (`<script`, `javascript:`, `on*=`, `<iframe`, `<object`, fenced code) plus an undefined "basic HTML" allowlist. Denylists are bypassable (`<embed>`, `<form action>`, `<svg onload>`, `<meta http-equiv=refresh>`, `data:` hrefs, CSS `url()`), so "cannot carry arbitrary executable content" (AC-1) is not actually enforced by spec — Gate 1.5's request was a closed allowlist, not a longer denylist.
MAJOR: Generator-authority check has no determinism contract: unless `gen_docs_index` output is pinned as stable (no timestamps, stable ordering, stable serialization), byte-diff validation yields flaky DERIVED_DOC_STALE or encourages reviewers to disable it — an integrity gate that cries wolf gets bypassed.
Grandfathering is open-ended (no expiry or one-time migration that rewrites legacy approvals into compliant records); the ordering invariant never becomes universally true.

review_scope (9 entries) and REVIEW_EXCLUDES/coverage path set are claimed to be "one path set" but no single config key or owner file is named in the design; two list literals in different scripts is exactly the divergence risk the previous MAJOR flagged.

Precheck gate count hard-coded as "49 gates" in requirements/test_matrix: adding any future gate breaks the test independent of this change; assert gate-set membership/completeness, not a literal count.
MINOR: Item-level `rollback: "Revert the change"` contradicts design_pack's 4-step rollback (revert, regenerate docs, re-run gates); the item record should carry the full ordered rollback.
`DESIGN_PACK_CONFIG` is declared in observability but absent from the failure matrix and from the test matrix — an error code that nothing triggers or tests will silently rot.
"Allow basic HTML" is not enumerated (which tags/attributes), so implementers will diverge on tables/headings vs unsafe constructs; list the permitted tag/attribute set explicitly.
cutoff "2026-10-08T00:00:00Z / commit 9dba2e3d" does not state how the tool resolves/validates the SHA if history is rewritten (shallow clone, rebase); define fallback behavior and its error code.
NIT: Performance bound "20MB/file cap" lacks stated behavior on breach (skip with warning vs gate fail) — pick fail-closed and note it.

Guardrails 2/3/4/8/9 are marked N/A for tooling but not stated as N/A in the design; one line of "not applicable: no scheduler, no authz boundary, no API, no tenant data" would silence future checklist re-litigation.
SUMMARY: Design v2 is a clear improvement: single content-class owner, pinned error codes, ancestry negatives, and a bounded local check address the Gate 1.5 findings in spirit.

Two residuals block acceptance: the grandfathering predicate is still non-deterministic (the exact defect the prior BLOCKER named), and AC-1's executable-content rule is specified as a bypassable denylist rather than a closed allowlist.
Secondary risks: generator determinism (flaky freshness gate), duplicated review-scope path sets, and a hard-coded precheck gate count that will break on unrelated changes.

rereview_reason: design v2 fixes all 1.5 findings; HIL material change
